THE EMBER CROWN

Prologue

The city burned every winter, and every winter the people of Ashfall rebuilt it
from the same grey stone, as if the fire were a season like any other and the
rebuilding were simply what one did when the snow came down off the mountains.
Nobody remembered a year without it, and nobody, in the end, asked why it came.

Chapter One

Mira reached the gate before dawn. The guards were asleep at their posts, wrapped
in their cloaks against the wind that came howling down the valley from the pass.
She slipped past them without a sound, her boots wrapped in rags to soften them.
Chapter one was the hardest, her teacher used to say, of any book worth reading.

* * *

    An indented line, kept as typed, because some writers indent their letters.

Inside, the market was already stirring. Bakers fed their ovens, and the smell
of bread drifted over the rooftops like a promise made to every hungry child.

CHAPTER 2: THE GATE

Rain fell on the black gate. It had fallen for three days, and it would fall for
three more, washing the soot from the walls and the courage from the guards.
#
The second scene starts after a lone hash, the way some writers mark a break.
